*PharmaCraft Daily - 28 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (General Pharmacology)
Q: The study of movement of drugs in the body (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion) is called?
Ans: Pharmacokinetics
Why: Pharmacokinetics = what the body does to the drug (ADME). Pharmacodynamics = what the drug does to the body.

🌍 *FMGE* (General Pharmacology)
Q: The 'therapeutic index' is the ratio of?
Ans: LD50/ED50
Why: Therapeutic index = LD50/ED50; a higher value means a safer drug.

🩺 *NEET PG* (General Pharmacology)
Q: A drug with a very high volume of distribution (Vd) is best described as?
Ans: Extensively bound to tissues
Why: A large Vd (e.g., chloroquine, amiodarone) indicates extensive tissue sequestration; haemodialysis removes little.

🏥 *INI-CET* (General Pharmacology)
Q: A drug has a clearance of 70 mL/min and is 100% bioavailable. To double the steady-state concentration you should?
Ans: Double the maintenance dose rate
Why: At steady state, Css is proportional to dosing rate/clearance; doubling the maintenance rate doubles Css.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper I: General/Experimental)
Q: In a Schild plot, the pA2 value represents the negative log of the antagonist concentration that requires?
Ans: A doubling of agonist concentration
Why: pA2 is the -log of the molar antagonist concentration that necessitates doubling the agonist concentration (dose ratio = 2).
